item.title: Ex-Cowboy Dez Bryant says officer pointed gun at him in front of daughters
item.description: Dallas wide receiver De Bryant (88) is pictured before the New Orleans Saints vs. the Dallas Cowboys NFL football game at Cowboys Stadium in Arlington on Sunday, December 23, 2012. (Louis DeLuca/The Dallas Morning News) (Louis DeLuca/Dallas Morning News) Former Dallas Cowboys star Dez Bryant says a Southlake police officer pointed a gun at him in front of his two daughters Sunday. Bryant was cited for assault after a confrontation with two men. Southlake police responded around 12:59 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 25, to reports of a fight involving multiple people in a retail parking lot in the 2200 block of FM 1709, according to an Oct. 26 news release from the Southlake Police Department. Southlake is a Dallas-Fort Worth suburb about 25 miles northwest of Dallas. Several callers reported a possible weapon, prompting officers to draw their firearms as a precaution when they arrived, according to police. Several people were temporarily detained during the investigation, but no firearms were recovered at the scene. The confrontation began as a traffic dispute near Kimball Avenue after Bryant said another driver cut him off, according to the release. Both parties went to a nearby parking lot, where the argument escalated into an alleged assault. Bryant was cited for assault by contact, a Class C misdemeanor, and released at the scene, according to police. ALSO READ: Stephen Jones expects Eagles to test Cowboys offense with heavy pressure packages Video Bryant provided to sports outlet OutKick shows the former Cowboys receiver lying on the ground in handcuffs alongside several other men as officers responded, according to WFAA . Bryant's girlfriend, who was there with his two daughters, recorded the video. Bryant also said one of the men threatened to shoot him before police arrived. An officer is seen holding a rifle in the video. Southlake police provided WFAA with a written statement but declined an interview. Bryant, a first-round pick by Dallas in the 2010 NFL Draft, became one of the Cowboys' most productive receivers during his eight seasons with the team, from 2010 to 2017. He earned three Pro Bowl selections and was named a first-team All-Pro in 2014, when he led the NFL with 16 touchdown receptions. Bryant finished his Cowboys career with 531 receptions for 7,459 yards and 73 touchdowns, ranking among the franchise's all-time receiving leaders. He later returned to the NFL with the Baltimore Ravens in 2020. His son, Dez Bryant Jr., is a standout wide receiver at Southlake Carroll High School. Bryant has frequently attended the team's games this season. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d'Or winner - but he wasn't only one
item.description: Harry Kane has become the first Englishman since 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or [Getty Images] Harry Kane was crowned winner of the men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night, but a few hours earlier that confirmation appeared to have been announced prematurely. At 17:15 GMT, an article from the award's official website titled 'Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or' began to circulate online. The widespread sharing of the article caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football - the organisers of the award - had fallen short at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, who was voted for by journalists at the end of September, under wraps. That was until further digging on the Ballon d'Or website revealed that some of the other favourites to win the award - including Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe - also had similar pieces penned and published about them. When asked about the articles by BBC Sport, a Ballon d'Or spokesperson said: "Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online. "These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings." By 17:40, the articles about Kane and Mbappe had been removed from the website. Similar articles were also written about London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona's Ewa Pajor. Putellas went on to be officially confirmed as the winner of the women's Ballon d'Or. That premature announcement may have sparked some excitement in Kane that this could be his year, but he only had to wait a little longer to find out for sure. item.description: Harry Kane is the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or for a quarter of a century (FRANCK FIFE) Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose trophy collection does not do justice to his remarkable talent and consistency. The Bayern Munich striker, 33, is the first Englishman to win football's most coveted individual honour since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane's numbers are staggering and the England captain appears to be improving with age, with 73 goals for club and country last season. In September he became the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, hitting the landmark on his 98th league appearance for Bayern. He is also Tottenham's all-time leading scorer with 280 goals, England's record scorer with 91, and the highest-scoring English player in the Champions League (58). But for all his personal achievements in club and international football, Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and was in England teams that twice lost the European Championship final. Kane's lethal finishing is not the only string to his bow. Honing an instinct he first developed as a youth team player, Kane has also blossomed into a gifted playmaker. "I feel like I've always had the passing range and the vision and the football brain -- the game understanding -- throughout my whole career, and I think that's just flourished these last couple of years especially, these last few years since I've been here at Bayern," he told UEFA.com. - Ageing like fine wine - The clean-cut Kane, married to his childhood sweetheart Katie Goodland, is an understated throwback in an era of football bling. But it has not always been plain sailing for a player who struggled to make an impression early in his career with Tottenham and was farmed out to other clubs on loan. There were almost two years between Kane's first Spurs goal, against Shamrock Rovers in 2011, and his next, against Hull in 2013. Even after his breakthrough season in 2014/15, he was dubbed a "one-season wonder", an accusation that has proved laughably wide of the mark. Bayern boss Vincent Kompany has spoken of Kane's numerous qualities, including his distribution, work rate and "game intelligence". item.title: Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend
item.description: Harry Kane broke Bayern Munich's goalscoring record for a season in his third campaign at the club [Getty Images] Harry Kane has become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others. Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom. Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three. "I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special," said an emotional Kane. "Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year. "[There are] some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations to all the winners and nominees tonight. [It is] an impressive showing of determination and what hard work can really achieve." England manager Thomas Tuchel said: "I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world. "To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader. "I know you will enjoy this moment with your loved ones and then get back to doing what you do best – scoring goals and winning football matches." Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals - plus eight assists - in 65 matches. Only one player at a club in Europe's top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season. But he wins it despite not lifting either of football's biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals. Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d'Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. To celebrate Kane's success, the Wembley arches were lit up in gold on Monday night. BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies. But in terms of individual output Kane - whose previous best Ballon d'Or finish was 10th - was unmatched last season. item.description: Bayern Munich's Harry Kane arrives to the red carpet ahead of the 70th annual Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre. (is associated with: «Kane wins 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or ahead of Mbappe and Yamal») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Harry Kane has become the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being honoured at London Palladium on Monday. Michael Owen was the last player from England to receive the prestigious individual accolade in 2001, but Kane's incredible 73-goal haul last season for club and country earned him the award from French magazine France Football. Bayern Munich forward Kane was a popular winner in the capital and has followed in the footsteps of Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen as a Ballon d'Or winner from England. Barcelona and Spain's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe provided strong competition for Kane and the trio were bizarrely announced as winners on the official website hours before the ceremony in London. Further chaos followed with the awards pushed back by 30 minutes to start at 8.30 pm (1930 GMT), but just over two hours later and Kane received the 70th Ballon d'Or to enormous cheers and chants of "Harry" inside the London Palladium, minutes after London City midfielder Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time. "Wow, I'm almost speechless," an emotional Kane said on stage. "First of all, thanks again to France Football and the Ballon d'Or for this amazing event. Being in London, it is extra special, it felt like a good omen. "Thank you to everyone for voting for me. I can imagine it was very tough. Thank you to everyone that voted for me." Kane, who thanked England, Bayern and former club Tottenham, said: "To my wife Kate, my best friend. We've been through ups and downs. You are my biggest support and I felt like you wanted this more than me. "The anxious wait ... Here it is, we done it and you always want the best for me. You sacrifice yourself to make me achieve my dreams. This wouldn't be possible without you and it is something we can celebrate, not me. We're a team. I can't wait to celebrate tonight. I love you. "My kids, sat home watching, it's definitely past your bedtime! To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry, you are the reason I do it. This is a special one and I can't wait to bring this home and celebrate with you. I love you very much." He added: "It's just the journey. For any young boy or girl who wants to achieve their dream, anything is possible. "I hope my journey, it wasn't straightforward, I didn't go straight to the top, I had to experience a lot of loan moves and fight my way to get to where I am now. I hope that can give you inspiration and thank you very much." item.title: Trae Young is doing exactly what Wizards need despite shooting woes
item.description: Trae Young is doing exactly what Wizards need despite shooting woes originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Trae Young's reputation as an impressive shot-maker precedes him. But in Wizards colors, he's found it much harder to get his shot to fall. The diminutive point guard is arguably best known for his trifecta, a shot that can prove glittering when wet. Young has three seasons with more than 200 three-pointers made in his career. He would likely have more had he been dealt some positive injury luck over the years. In 2026-27, though, his shot has looked far less lively. Young is shooting well under 40 percent from the field and a little over 30 percent from three. His scoring hasn't lived up to its billing thus far. And yet, there's a case to be made he has been vital to Washington's efforts as it attempts to climb up the Eastern Conference table. Here's why. Trae Young is doing exactly what Wizards need despite shooting woes To say Young is shooting poorly thus far would be an understatement. The Wizards guard is shooting a little over 36 percent on the year, seven percentage points below his career average. His 56.5 percent true shooting rate sits just 0.5 percent higher than the league-average rate, per Databallr, a disappointing mark given Young's reputation as an accomplished shooter from range. And yet, there's a case to be made that Young has been as effective as ever for 2-1 Washington. He leads the league in assists (11.3 per game), proving an excellent distributor to a Wizards side that has hopes to surge into relevancy in 2026-27. Young ranks in the 100th percentile in points created (47.7 per game) and rim assists (7.0). He also has kept his turnover numbers exceedingly low, surrendering the ball just 2.3 times per contest. Young's willingness to shoot from anywhere on the floor has drawn him admirers throughout his career. It's his playmaking that has proven especially valuable to Washington. With AJ Dybantsa yet to make his debut, there's even more dynamism to be unearthed within the Wizards' ranks. Young will be key to helping unlock that offensive potential — even if his shot isn't falling. MORE : Watch Wizards, Capitals and Mystics games on DAZN

item.title: Thunder lose starters Wallace and Williams to injuries
item.description: Oklahoma City Thunder starters Jalen Williams, left, and Cason Wallace, right, are out indefinitely after being injured in an NBA victory that boosted the team to a 3-0 start (Sam Hodde) Oklahoma City Thunder forward Jalen Williams and guard Cason Wallace will both be sidelined indefinitely after upcoming surgeries to repair injuries, the NBA club's general manager Sam Presti announced Monday. Williams suffered a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle while Wallace suffered a torn labrum in his left shoulder during Sunday's victory over the Los Angeles Clippers. A timetable for the return of both starters will not be determined until after the operations, but each is in jeopardy of missing the remainder of the NBA campaign based on similar past injuries. "We're extremely optimistic about the recovery for both of the players," Presti said at a news conference. "Most importantly, things could have been a lot worse." The Thunder started the NBA season 3-0 with solid contributions from both players. Williams has averaged 13.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.0 steals a game while Wallace has averaged 6.3 points, 2.3 rebounds, 2.3 steals and 1.3 assists a game. "We'll wrap our arms around these guys. We'll get them back. We'll get them healthy," Presti said. "When these things happen it's really tough. This is the kind of thing that gets thrown at you here. You just plow right through it. You walk through punches and you step over roadblocks. Our guys are ready to do that." Presti said he has not pondered what deals he could make to boost the Thunder's hopes for the campaign in the short term. "I really haven't given a lot of thought to that," Presti said. That included any thought of trying to coax former Thunder star point guard Russell Westbrook out of retirement. The 2017 NBA Most Valuable Player retired in August at age 37 after 18 NBA seasons, including 2008-2019 with the Thunder. "All I'm focused on right now is players, getting them the right support, and then helping everybody within our group," Presti said. "We have a tremendous challenge in front of us but this is what we do. We'll have to keep grinding and I know that's what we'll do." Williams landed awkwardly and his left leg collapsed with 74 seconds remaining in the game. He was carried off on a stretcher, teammates in tears. Williams signed a five-year contract extension worth $239 million last year after playing through the Thunder's title run with a torn right wrist ligament. "That's what keeps him motivated." Wallace, who signed a five-year contract extension worth $139 million last week, was injured in the first quarter after running into a moving screen. Patrick Mahomes continues to struggle against elite defenses, raising concerns for the Kansas City Chiefs That problem is that he's just struggling when up against elite defenses. "Patrick Mahomes simply looked off all night long and continued his struggles playing against top-ranked defenses," he notes in the piece. item.title: The Case for the Los Angeles Dodgers to Re-Sign Tarik Skubal
item.description: Though he was with the Dodgers only a few months, starting pitcher Tarik Skubal sparked the star-studded roster, and while bringing him back likely requires a huge contract , the Dodgers would be remiss to let him go. What does Tarik Skubal mean to the Dodgers? The lefty, who won the American League Cy Young Award in both 2024 and 2025, met the massive expectations placed on him when he joined the Dodgers just before the trade deadline. Yes, the Dodgers failed in their quest for a third straight championship, but a shaky bullpen and an inability to consistently drive in runners in scoring position were largely to blame. Sep 17, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal celebrates after clinching the National League West title after the game against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images Per Baseball Reference , Skubal started 10 regular-season games for the Dodgers, averaging more than six innings per outing and posting a 5-2 record with a 2.61 ERA. His two playoff starts were a bit more uneven, with his dominant Game 1 start against the Atlanta Braves in the National League Division Series setting the stage for the Dodgers’ series win. In that game, he allowed one run over six innings, striking out seven and giving up two hits and two walks. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Eight days later, he started Game 1 of the NLCS, but this time he gave up two runs in five innings, a hurdle his offense couldn’t clear. Despite the rough end to the season, Skubal has more than shown he can succeed in LA. Would Tarik Skubal come back to the Dodgers? For Skubal, money will certainly be a factor. He’s reportedly looking at a long-term deal worth about $40 million per year over seven or so seasons . The Dodgers could offer that kind of contract, especially before a potential lockout and maybe a salary cap, but more than that, they can offer Skubal consistency and winning baseball. item.title: Harry Kane Makes History as Just Fourth Englishman to Win Ballon d’Or Award
item.description: Getty Images The winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or is Harry Kane . Kane, 33, was crowned on Monday, October 26, as soccer’s biggest stars gathered in London for the 70th annual awards ceremony. The prestigious prize, presented by France Football magazine since 1956, recognizes the best player in men’s soccer, with a panel of journalists from the top 100-ranked countries in the sport voting on the winner. The award marked the first Ballon d’Or for the FC Bayern Munich striker and captain of the England national football team, who was emotional as he held up the coveted prize, making him just one of four English players to ever win the award. “First of all, I’m almost speechless. Being here in London as well has made it extra special and looked like a good omen for me tonight, so thank you very much. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year, some of the incredible players I was up against, some of my teammates, some world-class players in the room tonight,” Kane gushed, thanking both his Bayern Munich and England teammates. “Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees tonight. An impressive showing of what determination and hard work can really achieve, so well done.” Kane finished the speech by thanking his wife, Kate Goodland , their four children, and her family, as well as his parents, for the instrumental role they’ve played in his career. Getty Images Kane was presented with the award by Brazilian legend Ronaldo Luís Nazário de Lima , mononymously known as Ronaldo, who was also given his flowers Monday night with a tribute ahead of the trophy presentation. Host Thierry Henry also congratulated Kane following the win, praising his work ethic and calling him a “worthy winner.” In addition to winning the Ballon d’Or, Kane also took home the Striker of the Year trophy Monday. Lionel Messi , who holds the record with eight Ballon d’Or wins, was also in contention, along with Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe and FC Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal . item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or win doesn’t erase past robberies, but it eases the sting
item.description: (Photo by Rico Brouwer/Soccrates/Getty Images) | Getty Images Harry Kane winning the Ballon d’Or does not make up for Robert Lewandowski and Franck Ribéry getting hosed in their respective races for football’s biggest individual honor, but it certainly eases the sting a little. Bayern Munich supporters have long memories, and the frustration surrounding those two snubs is not going anywhere. Ribéry looked destined to win the award in 2013 after he lping Bayern Munich complete an extraordinary treble, only to watch Cristiano Ronaldo take home the prize. Despite Ribéry’s enormous contrib utions to one of the greatest teams in club football, the Frenchman was left empty-handed. Then came Lewandowski. The Polish striker delivered a rguably the most frustrating Ballon d’Or injustice of them all in 2020, when the award was canceled en tirely because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Lewandowski had enjoyed a sensational season, leading Bayern Munich to the Champions Lea gue, Bundesliga, and DFB-Pokal titles while scoring goals at a ridiculous rate. The award was never presented, leaving him witho ut the recognition he deserved. You could also argue that Lewandowski deserved the award in 2021 when he broke t he Bundesliga go alscoring record. Kane’s triumph cannot rewrite either of those chapters. Ribéry will always be a Ballon d’Or winner in the eyes of Bayern Munich supporters, and Lewandowski’s 2020 and 2021 campaigns deserve their own place in football history. Still, seeing Kane receive this recognition is a meaningful moment for Bayern Munich. The Englishman has produced an outstanding season, and his achievement reinforces that players can reach the very top of the individual game in Munich. He netted 61 goals in 51 appearances for the German club last season, contributing to yet another Bundesliga title, as well as a German Cup triumph. item.title: Kane beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d'Or glory
item.description: Spain's Luis de La Fuente won the men's coach of the year (FRANCK FIFE) Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. "Without you guys (his Bayern Munich team-mates) and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much," he said after collecting the award. Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football. "Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level. "Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added. - Putellas back on top - Winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return back to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season. "Ever since I suffered the injury, I've been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it'll happen again," Putellas told AFP in an interview last month. item.title: If it’s 2 hours before Brewers game time, you could be playing chess with Jake Bauers
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL – There are numerous apps out there where you can play chess with someone – a real person, not AI – on your phone. And games can be fast-paced and intense, or can evolve over long stretches of time. That’s the beauty of it. And before games, Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers ’ way of locking in, and blocking out the distractions, is with the help of one of these apps. “I'm probably going to be sitting in the hot tub playing chess until about 30 minutes before the game,” Bauers said. “Throw my uniform on, go out there, and see what happens.” That means in the afternoon hours of Monday, Oct. 26, someone else in the world, maybe from Newport Beach, California, maybe from New York City, was playing chess with the MVP of the NL Championship Series – and had no idea their opponent was getting ready for Game 3 of the World Series. “Yeah, I've got a random username,” Bauers said. “I don't know who I'm playing; they surely don't know who they're playing. “It's not like I'm any good! It's not something special. I make my fair share of mistakes. It's just keep my mind occupied, kill time, all that for sure.” Bauers is having a full-circle moment anyway. He made his major-league debut here in June 2018, when he was called up by the Rays. Bauers made a nice defensive grab for an out in his first game and then he got a nice single for his first hit in that first series. The road ahead for Bauers became tough, though, after that first year in Tampa Bay, which went 90-72. He would end up playing for five teams before he landed with the Brewers in 2024. Then, in Milwaukee with a changing role, he contemplated retiring . Milwaukee Brewers memorabilia Instead, Bauers has constantly evolved as a person and that evolution helped him as a player. “I used to put so much pressure on myself that it became almost unbearable,” Bauers said. “I used to want it so bad that I was just forcing it away from myself in a sense.” But in his career, and in his three years in Milwaukee, he changed. He worked on his own personal narrative. “I'm here to experience whatever comes at me,” he said, “and I'm going to make the most of it − good, bad, pretty, ugly, just irrelevant. I'm here to experience it all.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: If it’s 2 hours before Brewers game time, you could be playing chess with Jake Bauers Our editors independently choose our recommendations.
